system.summary: Letter-position book cipher (counted as homophonic): pair a,b is letter b of line a of a rhymed German Lord's Prayer of eight lines, so each letter has many cells.
system.notes: Pairs written 'a,b.' inline in German or Latin clear text, words often closed by a vertical stroke; the writer may take any occurrence of a letter in the verse and scans forward along a line. Symbols = distinct number pairs. The verse: 'O Vatter aller frommen / geheiligt werd dein nahm / las dein reich zu uns kommen / dein will der mach uns zahm / gib brod vergib die sund / kein args das hertz entzunde / los uns aus aller nott / p?x'. About 3% of pairs are neighbouring-cell slips by the writer.

prior_solution.where: A contemporary Latin outline of letter 004 (the eight points and the closing question), on a slip filmed beside it in the same file. No edition, study or modern decipherment found by web search.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: the user picked the target from the catalogue and asked for it to be started in a worktree off origin/main; after a session break said 'continue'. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: solve.py (homophonic annealer, Latin 5-gram, optional key-text model)

solution.what: Web searches (German and English) for an edition or decipherment of the Erbach-Ludwig VI letters.

Found the open Arcinsys image URLs through the DDB API EDM record (Archivportal-D page is behind a bot check); downloaded 78 images of D 4 Nr. 248/3 and the candidate key files D 4 Nr. 141/2 and 239/1.
Two survey agents viewed all 78 images; only three 1666 letters (images 003, 004, 006 and refilmings) carry cipher.
Viewed the Hesse-Darmstadt key file 141/2 and Ludwig VI's notes 239/1 (images 000-107); found a 1640s homophonic number table and decipherments, not this system.
Transcribed letter 004 (571 pairs) from rotated, enlarged microfilm crops.
Row maxima 19-24 and rising runs inside one row point to a (line, letter) book cipher on an eight-line key text.
Homophonic anneal over 124 cells with a Latin 5-gram and a letter-frequency penalty.

Aligned the contemporary Latin outline slip with the frame words of letter 004: 'turbulentus', 'defectus', then 'dominus cui deus salutem ecclesie', 'conscientie et offensione dei', 'mercenariorum', 'oves suas', 'periculis'.
Anneal with 40-80 crib cells fixed; filled phrases such as 'status publicus', 'consiliis juvenilibus'.
Letters in the same key row spelled German words ('dein will ... uns', 'las dein reich zu uns', 'los uns aus aller not'); recognised a rhymed Lord's Prayer and rebuilt all eight lines.
Deciphered all three letters with the verse key unchanged; 591 of 610 pairs read as the key gives them, 19 neighbouring-cell slips corrected by sense.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 610 tokens, 123 types, la order 4: reading -2.39 per letter; random keys -4.598 (z 10.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.589 (mean -2.641, z 5.8); annealer on the real text -2.599. Verdict: pass.
Transcribed the clear German and Latin frame of the three letters from the microfilm (clear_text.md); No. 2 refers to a letter of 'rationes', dating the reasons letter before 27 Apr 1666.

Read share measured over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026): plain type of the readings counted and the italic clear frame left out, holes by words with the v2_score rules, one hole per word (a word with two blots counts once). L004 0.914 (117 words read, 11 holes, 128 cipher words: letters the writer left out, ink blots, one run); L003 and L006 1.0. L004 had been marked read with no read_share; its whole reading body was already 0.856. So the move of L004 to read in part, and of the class from read to read in part, comes from the existing read bar, not from the cipher-words rule. fraction_read (591 of 610 pairs) is unchanged.

Gap lines for letter 004 restated from what the files show. The [X] places are the transcription's mark for an ink blot or deliberate deletion on the film: blocker illegible. The five letters with no pair in ct_004.txt (the pairs run on with no gap, divider or [X]; the reading marks them as the writer's omissions, not re-checked on the film for this purpose) and the [..] before 'itum' (it follows the writer's divider directly, so nothing is missing in the transcription) are no longer listed as open pieces with a blocker; they still count as holes in the read share. The earlier needs-physical-access line is withdrawn.

texts.label: Letter 004, undated [before 27 Apr 1666], two pages
texts.summary: Erbach gives Ludwig VI eight reasons why he cannot leave his county: the troubled Empire, the electors' war nearby, his wife's illness, his brothers taking up government by connivance and a dispensation of age, their youthful counsels, his subjects' trust, the division of property, and disloyal councillors. He asks whether a lord may abandon church, subjects, house and wife and 'put his sheep under hirelings' (John 10:12). No. 2 (27 Apr 1666) refers to this letter of 'rationes', so it predates it.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences: every cipher passage forms Latin or German sense with its clear frame (clear_text.md, transcribed from the microfilm); 15 neighbouring-cell slips corrected and listed; some frame words marked [?] or [..]. _check_reading.py (27 Oct) scores reading_004.md at 0.35 clean with a German word list: the passages are mostly Latin, and the edition's slip marks, blots and [?] frame words count as holes; read by eye, every cipher passage forms a sentence.

texts.note: 16 Nov 2026: read share over cipher words only 0.914: 128 cipher words (plain type in reading_004.md, the clear frame in italics left out), 117 read and 11 holes counted by words. Four carry a letter the writer left out: folgende[n], nich[t], statu[s], [ru]m. Five have an ink blot: co⟨n⟩[X]ventum, sche[X]rts[X]s, elector[X]um, fidelita[X]tis, and the [X] after fratribus. One has both: urs[X]ache[n]. One is the run [..]itum. The neighbouring-cell slips marked ⟨x⟩ count as read, as before. The entry had no read_share, and the whole reading body (clear frame included) was already 0.856, under the bar. So the change from read to read in part comes from the read bar as it stood before 16 Nov, not from the cipher-words rule.
